title: About Public AI Inventory - Endpoint AI

blocks.text: The Public AI Inventory for Endpoint AI apps helps you manage AI risk by giving you a structured, continuously updated view of the AI applications installed or used on endpoints.
The Public AI Inventory Endpoint AI Page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Identify which endpoint AI apps are present and being used across devices and users.
Group apps by category and focus first on higher-risk types, e.g., chat, remote-assist, file-sharing–heavy apps.
Monitor whether controls reduce risky app adoption and overall exposure.

blocks.heading: About the Endpoint AI Apps Page

blocks.text: On the Public AI-Inventory - Endpoint AI page (Public AI > App Inventory > Endpoint AI), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Filter the report for the Last 1 Day, Last 7 Days, Last 15 Days, Last Month, or Last Quarter.
Total Endpoint AI Apps: View the total number of Endpoint AI apps that are in use in the organization.
Instances: View the number of detected application instances.
Top Endpoint AI Apps: View the top 5 Endpoint AI apps by instances.
Endpoint AI Apps by Category: View the distribution of the endpoint AI apps by their functional classifications.
Search for Endpoint AI application by name.
View a list of all the Endpoint AI applications. For each application, you can view:
Name: Name of the Endpoint AI App. Click the app name to view additional details.
Instances: The number of detected application instances.
Versions: The number of available application versions.
Overview: View the following information for the app:
Application Name
Category
Company
Product Name
Operating Platform
Original Filename
Application Type
Executable Filename
The Versions table displays the following information:
Version Number: View the available application versions.
Code Signing Certificate Status: The code signing status of the application, i.e., Valid Signature, Certificate Expired, Unsigned, Not Valid, or Invalid Signature.
MD5: The MD5 hash of the application.
Threat Type: The threat type of the application, i.e., Benign, Malicious, Suspicious, or Unknown.
Category: The functional classification used to group the application.
Total Instances: The total number of application instances discovered.
Versions: The number of application versions available.
